# HAttachment

> File artifacts with preview/download/removal requests and processing states.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HAttachment` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-attachment>`.
- Constructor: `HearthAttachmentElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Developer.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HAttachment.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Display-only artifact UI; the app owns upload, download URLs, preview handling and removal. preview/remove emit requests. href and previewSrc accept safe HTTP(S)/relative links and application-owned blob URLs; the application owns Blob URL revocation. Native download behavior remains browser-controlled, especially cross-origin. Upload progress is supplied by the app; processing/error/done have visible state labels.

## Public API

name, href, previewSrc, description: string · size, progress: number · state: idle | uploading | processing | error | done · removable: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    name: string;
    href?: string;
    previewSrc?: string;
    size?: number;
    description?: string;
    state?: "idle" | "uploading" | "processing" | "error" | "done";
    progress?: number;
    removable?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ state: "done" }
```

### Events

preview(), remove()

```ts
type Emits = {
    remove: [
    ];
    preview: [
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, preview

Use `hearth-attachment::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HAttachment } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
function remove() { /* Update the application-owned attachment list. */ }
</script>

<template>
  <HAttachment name="build-report.json" :size="4096" description="Build artifact" state="done" href="/artifacts/build-report.json" removable @remove="remove" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-attachment');
Object.assign(element, {
  "name": "build-report.json",
  "size": 4096,
  "description": "Build artifact",
  "state": "done",
  "href": "/artifacts/build-report.json",
  "removable": true
});

element.addEventListener('preview', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
